# Miqsat Ma'ase Ha-Torah Section 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 4QMMT (4Q394–399, Cave 4), Section C | **Condition:** Fragmentary; reconstructed from multiple manuscripts

---

**6:1** You know very well that we have no treachery, no deceit, and no wrongdoing on our hands, because for [these matters] we are willing to [...]

**6:2** [...] Indeed, we are writing to you [...] for your benefit and for the benefit of your people [...]

**6:3** [...] because we can see that you are a person of wisdom who understands the Torah. Think carefully about [...]

**6:4** [...] everything that has happened to you [...] and you will realize [...]

**6:5** [And in]deed, we have [written] to you about some of the practices required by the Torah that we believe are for your good and for your people's good, because we recognized that you have wisdom and knowledge of the Torah.

**6:6** Think carefully about all these things and ask God to set your thinking straight and to keep you far from wicked plots and the schemes of Belial,

**6:7** so that in the end you will have reason to rejoice, when you see that some of what we have said turns out to be true.

**6:8** And it will be credited to you as a righteous act when you do what is right and good in God's sight — for your own good and for the good of Israel.

**6:9** [...] because [...] in the books of Moses it is written [...] and in the prophetic writings [...]

**6:10** [...] that the blessings arrived [...] during the reign of Solomon, David's son [...] and the curses as well [...]

**6:11** [...] which came from the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat all the way to the exile of Jerusalem under Zedekiah, king of Judah [...]

**6:12** [...] that God will bring upon them [...] and it is written [...] in the books of Moses and in the [prophetic] writings that [...]

**6:13** [...] [the bles]sings came during the time of David and Solomon [...] and the curses came from [...] until [...]

**6:14** [...] and we can see that some of the blessings and curses recorded in the books of [Moses] have already taken place [...]

**6:15** This is the final era, when the people will return to Israel for[ever ...] and never turn away again [...]

**6:16** [...] but the wicked will continue to act [...] and [...] remember [...]

**6:17** Call to mind the kings of Israel and reflect on what they did: every king who honored [the To]rah was rescued from his troubles;

**6:18** those were the ones who sought to follow the Torah, and their sins were forgiven.

**6:19** Think of David — he was a man known for his faithful deeds, and he too was rescued from many troubles and received forgiveness.

**6:20** We have also written to you about some of the practices required by the Torah [...] so that it may benefit you [...]

**6:21** [...] because [...] you will receive [...] at the end of time [...] when you live with integrity before God [...]

**6:22** [...] and it will be credited to you as righteousness [...] for doing what is upright and good in His sight [...]

**6:23** [...] for your good and for the good of Israel [...]

**6:24** [...] and it is written: [...] in the final days [...]

**6:25** [...] and remember everything that Moses, God's servant, said [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Section C is the emotional and theological heart of MMT. "Credited to you as a righteous act" (6:8) renders the pivotal phrase dynamically — the Hebrew echoes Gen 15:6, but PNEUMA emphasizes that the "reckoning" is based on action, not abstract faith. "Practices required by the Torah" again renders ma'ase ha-torah for clarity. "Wicked plots and the schemes of Belial" pairs two near-synonyms dynamically. The historical examples are rendered with temporal markers ("during the reign of") rather than the Hebrew "in the days of." "Faithful deeds" for chasidei ma'asim connects David's character to covenant loyalty. The letter's closing refrain — Torah obedience brings blessing, Torah faithfulness is counted as righteousness — drives home the document's central argument with passionate conviction.*
